newsitem.title: USA: Merrill keeps underweight recommendation on Peru.
newsitem.headline: Merrill keeps underweight recommendation on Peru.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co said Friday it was maintaining an underweight recommendation on Peru's when-issued Brady bonds due to recent political factors, expected further delays on the Brady closing, and the likelihood of disappointing growth figures for 1996.

"We have had an underweight recommendation on Peru for most of 1996, and we maintain that position in light of the recent political developments and several other factors," Joyce Chang, director of emerging markets at Merrill Lynch, said in a daily research report.

While the significant drop in the price of Peru's when-issued Brady bonds as a result of the guerrilla attack on the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima should not be long-lasting, Merrill said it is maintaining an underweight recommendation.
It said it expects that delays on the Brady agreement could extend beyond the first quarter of 1997.

"The government has stated that due to complications in the reconciliation process that are taking longer than anticipated to resolve, the closing of the Brady deal could be delayed into the first quarter of 1997. We believe the closing could be delayed even further, although deal completion risk does not appear to have increased," Chang said.

The Merrill report also said that on December 16 the World Bank board of directors delayed a $483 million disbursement to help finance the costs of the Brady closing and another $100 million for general balance of payments assistance.

"No motive for the delay was given, but such a move is highly unusual. Given this delay and the fact that attention will be focused on the hostage situation and upcoming talks with Ecuador on the border conflict, further delays to the Brady closing cannot be ruled out," Chang said.
Concerns that tensions with Ecuador could rise in January added to Merrill's underweight recommendation.

"While we do not believe that a large-scale offensive is likley to be resumed by either country, the recent purchase of MIGs by the Peruvian military has increased anti-Peruvian rhetoric in Ecuador and could lead to a flare-up in the tensions between the two countries over the short-term," she said in the report.
In addition, Merrill said concerns over a resurgence in terrorism may increase as some rebel leaders who were incarcerated in the early 1990s are scheduled to be released starting this year.
"Although a strong resurgence in terrorist activity is unlikely as a result of these releases, the organizational capacity of the Shining Path and the MRTA could be improved slightly," Chang said.
